title: Activation Hold Term Calculation — Homesite Reservation
content:
**Calculation clause.** The activation hold term of a Homesite Reservation is worked out as the activation start offset plus the activation hold length plus the activation lender bonus, less the activation letter shortening and less the activation card shortening, all in whole calendar days; the sum is then held to at most the class's maximum total hold days, and no part of it is rounded.

The hold is counted from the reservation date, so the activation start offset is zero. The activation hold length is the class's initial hold days. The activation lender bonus, the activation letter shortening and the activation card shortening are each zero days. The activation hold term is therefore the class's initial hold days, a whole number of days that needs no rounding.

## Elements of the term

| Element | Value | Effect on the term |
|---|---|---|
| Activation start offset | zero (the hold is counted from the reservation date) | added |
| Activation hold length | the class's initial hold days | added |
| Activation lender bonus | zero days | added |
| Activation letter shortening | zero days | subtracted |
| Activation card shortening | zero days | subtracted |
| Cap | the class's maximum total hold days | the term is the lower of the sum and the cap |

The initial hold days and the maximum total hold days are those of the reservation's premium class.

## Worked example (hypothetical class figures: initial hold days 12, maximum total hold days 20)

1. Sum: zero plus 12 plus zero, less zero and less zero, is 12 days.
2. Cap: 12 is not more than 20, so the activation hold term is 12 days.
3. A reservation dated 2 March therefore receives a hold expiry date of 14 March.

## Points of judgement

- The term is counted in whole calendar days from the reservation date; no part of it is rounded.
- The cap applies to the finished sum, after every addition and subtraction.
